proof_summary: Split the factorial ratios into their multiples-of-[1mp[0m and [1mp[0m-free parts, pair the latter by \(x\leftrightarrow p^r-x\), and truncate the resulting product in elementary symmetric sums; Faulhaber/power-sum identities show the first symmetric coefficient is divisible by \(p^r\) (by \(3^{r-1}\) when \(p=3\)) and the second by \(p\) for \(p\ge5\). Telescoping the same products gives \(p^3\mid 2\binom{3p^{r-1}}{p^{r-1}}^2-9\binom{2p^{r-1}}{p^{r-1}}\) (with the base case computed separately at \(p=3\)); these bounds make every surviving expansion term divisible by the target power, after which the coprime \(p\)-free product is canceled.
